## Chi-squared Probabilities.

In this tool, you input a $\chi^2$ score and the degrees of freedom, and get a corresponding $p$-value.

```{=html}
<iframe width="100%" height="500" src="../apps/Chi2calculator1.R"></iframe>
```

## Chi-square Quantiles (Critical values).

In this tool, you input a probability and degrees of freedom, and get a corresponding $X^2$ score.

```{=html}
<iframe width="100%" height="500" src="../apps/Chi2calculator1.R"></iframe>
```

For $\chi^2$ tests, one almost always looks at upper tail, and rarely
look at the lower tail (does the data fit better than expected).
Two-tailed tests are never ("What never?", "No Never!", "What Never?",
"Well hardly ever!", Gilbert & Sulivan, _HMS Pinfore_) done.
